stem: (Select TWO.) Larkspur Bank's root module needs the ID of a subnet that a child module creates internally as `aws_subnet.main`. The child is called with the label `network`. Which two statements about getting that ID are accurate?

choices.text: The child module has to declare an `output` block whose value is that subnet's ID
The root can read it as `module.network.aws_subnet.main.id`, because the child's resources are shared with its caller
A `locals` block in the child holding the ID is enough for the root to read it as `module.network.subnet_id`
The root reads the exposed value as `module.network.<output_name>`
A `variable` block in the child with the ID as its default lets the root read it as `module.network.subnet_id`

rationale: A child module exposes a value to its parent only through an output block, and the parent reads it with the `module.<label>.<output name>` syntax. A child's resources form a self-contained group, so the parent has no documented way to reach a resource address inside it. A locals block is confined to the module that defines it, so it is not readable from the parent. A variable block is an input that the parent sets, not a value the child hands back.
